hook.text: Two hospitals want to train an AI on their combined patient data. But neither can share the raw records. Now what?

buildup.text: Privacy-preserving computation lets parties compute on data they can't see. The data stays encrypted during processing.

discovery.text: Techniques include homomorphic encryption, secure enclaves, and federated learning — all emerging in cloud services.

twist.text: These techniques are still slow. Homomorphic encryption can be millions of times slower than normal computing.

climax.text: As regulation tightens, privacy-preserving computation will become essential. The technology is catching up to the need.

punchline.text: Compute on data you can't see. Privacy and insight coexist.

quiz.question: What is the main limitation of privacy-preserving computation today?
options: The techniques are extremely slow and computationally expensive
It only works with numerical data, not text or images
Cloud providers have banned all privacy-preserving techniques

details.summary: Privacy-preserving computation allows analysis of sensitive data without exposing it. Techniques include homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation, and differential privacy. These enable collaboration on confidential datasets like healthcare records and financial data.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations hold valuable data they cannot share due to privacy regulations. Privacy-preserving computation unlocks insights from sensitive data without violating privacy laws.
takeaways: Analyzes data without exposing the underlying records
Enables cross-organization collaboration on confidential data
Techniques include homomorphic encryption and differential privacy

faq.question: What is homomorphic encryption?
faq.answer: Homomorphic encryption allows computation on encrypted data without decrypting it first. The results, when decrypted, match what would have been produced on the plaintext. It is computationally expensive but enables processing sensitive data safely in untrusted environments.

faq.question: Is privacy-preserving computation practical today?
faq.answer: Differential privacy is widely used by Apple, Google, and the US Census. Secure multi-party computation is deployed in finance. Fully homomorphic encryption remains slow for general use but is practical for specific operations. The field is advancing rapidly.
